box.note: The first engine: three.js r186 with RoundedBoxGeometry, Reflector, BufferGeometryUtils and SkeletonUtils; the box's second lock; recipes as scripts named by their BLAKE3 hash, built with their declared parameters, handed back as plain data (format 0) and a card (v1)
Each picture goes out once (box data format 1): textures name the picture they show in images, so a picture shared by many textures, as the kit's are, crosses once and is kept once

Controls: each control a built object offers (a tent's pitch, a pickup's doors and tailgate, a bag's open, a fire lit, a sealed asset's explode and build) is played in the box from 0 to 1 and leaves as numbers (box data format 2), with the object as built put back first; and each material with the kit's section caps says how its cut face looks (its colour, roughness and metalness)

Engine 4: what a viewer needs of a build as data (format 3: parts, labels, shells, cut, solver readings and moves, clips and poses), skinned actors with their skins, builds kept running in the box (live, tick, break, mend, end), rig catalogs on cards (their ids written as a card's); each control set back to its rest after its bake, so a mesh it reshapes leaves as built

Engine 5 (format 4): an actor's clips played in the box and written down as tables on its view (box/clips.js: clips in time over 32 s, gaits by pace, distance and turn), for the page to play any number of copies by (../clips.js playerOf); lights leave as lights; and what else a control or a running build's step changes, only where it changes: the meshes it reshapes (positions and normals), material looks (colour, glow, opacity, roughness, metalness) and lights (colour, brightness, reach, fall-off); a dug patch's setWet a control (wet)

logic.note: The first logic engine: QuickJS (quickjs-emscripten, single file) and the logic core, behind the shell's second lock; code as a JS module with no buffers, a seeded Math.random and a frozen Date, work counted in ticks, called as call, see, hook or view with one JSON text in and out

lib-three.note: three.js r186 with OrbitControls, MapControls, TrackballControls, RoundedBoxGeometry, ConvexGeometry, BufferGeometryUtils, SkeletonUtils, ImprovedNoise, SimplexNoise, Sky, RoomEnvironment and Line2 for a draw script

lib-d3.note: d3 7.9.0 for a draw script, as a module and as the global d3

lib-mcp-apps.note: The MCP Apps SDK (@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps 2.0.3, its dependencies bundled) for a draw script

view.note: The first view engine: a view's HTML made safe and drawn from its state, our components, charts and look, its draw script in a worker
Templates work through the sanitizer: a <template>'s each, as and if attributes are kept (v1 dropped them, so loops and conditions drew nothing)
Template attributes filled from the state pass the sanitizer again: a value that names a script, a handler or an address it may not is dropped before the element has it, and style is cleaned (G8)

A view's script is held to a budget of work (G7): the watch, a worker of ours beside the view's that nothing of the view's reaches, asks it at moments no script can foresee and counts how long each answer waits; 5 s of work in hand, refilled by half the time that passes. Past half of it the view's animation frames are spaced out (100 ms, 500 ms, then 2 s apart), and past all of it the view's worker is ended, as one that holds it 4 s without a break is

view-worker.note: The first view worker: a draw script on a linkedom DOM mirrored into the frame, canvases as ImageBitmaps, MCP Apps over parent.postMessage, module imports as lookups

A view's worker answers the watch (its beat port) as soon as it is free, with nothing of the view's script able to bend the answer, and spaces its animation frames out when the frame asks it to (pace, up to 2 s apart), so a scene too heavy for the machine slows down instead of being stopped
takes WebAssembly off the view's worker: WebKit compiled it despite the frame's policy

math.note: The first math engine: KaTeX 0.16.22 behind the shell's second lock, with WebAssembly taken off its worker too (WebKit compiles it despite the frame's policy), LaTeX in and MathML out, nothing else: MathML only (no styles, fonts, SVG or CSS), trust off, strict, a command it doesn't know or refuses (\href, \url, \includegraphics, \html…) and any error making no formula; each formula with macros of its own, at most 200 expansions and sizes of 10 em; 4,000 characters a formula, 1,000 formulas and 4 s of work a batch
